subject: ss-cardiology
title: Acyanotic Congenital Heart Disease in Adults

steps.tx: **Secundum atrial septal defect** is the most common adult congenital cardiac anomaly, located at the **fossa ovalis**, amenable to percutaneous transcatheter device closure if adequate margins of at least 5 mm exist around the defect. Left-to-right shunting produces right ventricular volume overload and wide, fixed splitting of the second heart sound.
steps.say: Secundum atrial septal defect is the most common adult congenital cardiac anomaly, located at the fossa ovalis, amenable to percutaneous transcatheter device closure if adequate margins of at least 5 mm exist around the defect. Left-to-right shunting produces right ventricular volume overload and wide, fixed splitting of the second heart sound.

rows: Surgical patch closure + mitral cleft repair

steps.tx: Color Doppler shows blood crossing a hole in the mid septum at the fossa ovalis from left atrium to right atrium. The shunt fills the right ventricle beyond capacity and flattens the septum into a D shape in diastole. Recognizing this **shunt** pattern links the murmur and fixed split sound to later **overload** and guides timely **closure** planning before pressures rise.
steps.say: The echo shows flow crossing a secundum defect between the atria. That extra flow loads the right ventricle and flattens the septum, which you see in the inset as an enlarged chamber with a D shaped profile. This pattern explains the classic murmur with a fixed split second sound. Spotting it early matters because a persistent shunt can progress and closure planning depends on defect size and surrounding rims.

vis.alt: Color Doppler shows flow across a secundum septal defect with an inset of enlarged right ventricle and flattened septum.
vis.caption: Echo shows shunt flow plus signs of right ventricular volume load. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Primum ASD** occurs in the inferior interatrial septum near AV valves as a component of partial AV septal defect, displaying marked **left axis deviation** on ECG and a cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet causing **mitral regurgitation**. Conduction system displacement predisposes to first-degree and advanced atrioventricular block.
steps.say: Primum ASD occurs in the inferior interatrial septum near AV valves as a component of partial AV septal defect, displaying marked left axis deviation on ECG and a cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet causing mitral regurgitation. Conduction system displacement predisposes to first-degree and advanced atrioventricular block.

left.title: Primum ASD Features
points: Defect located in inferior interatrial septum
Marked left axis deviation on 12-lead ECG
Associated with cleft anterior mitral leaflet
Requires surgical patch closure and valvuloplasty

right.title: Secundum ASD Features
points: Defect located in mid-septum at fossa ovalis
Right axis deviation and incomplete RBBB on ECG
Mitral valve apparatus is typically normal
Percutaneous catheter closure is treatment of choice

steps.tx: **Sinus venosus ASD** is situated near the SVC-RA junction and is strongly associated with **partial anomalous pulmonary venous return** of right upper pulmonary veins into the superior vena cava. Surgical patch repair reroutes anomalous pulmonary venous drainage into the left atrium while closing the interatrial communication.

Surgical patch repair reroutes anomalous pulmonary venous drainage into the left atrium while closing the interatrial communication.

nodes.label: Sinus Venosus Defect Located at SVC-RA Junction
Partial Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return of Right Upper Veins
Transesophageal Echo or Cardiac MRI Staging
Surgical Repair (Single/Double Patch or Warden Procedure)

steps.tx: **Ventricular septal defect** classification comprises **perimembranous** accounting for **70%** to **80%**, muscular trabecular, inlet AV canal type, and outlet **supracristal** defects predisposing to aortic valve prolapse and aortic regurgitation. The Venturi effect from high-velocity supracristal jetting draws the right coronary cusp into the defect.
steps.say: Ventricular septal defect classification comprises perimembranous accounting for 70% to 80%, muscular trabecular, inlet AV canal type, and outlet supracristal defects predisposing to aortic valve prolapse and aortic regurgitation. The Venturi effect from high-velocity supracristal jetting draws the right coronary cusp into the defect.

rows: Most common; adjacent to conduction tissue and septal TV leaflet
Entirely surrounded by muscle; high rate of spontaneous closure
Posterior beneath AV valves; common in trisomy 21
Beneath semilunar valves; triggers progressive aortic regurgitation

steps.tx: Significant **left-to-right shunt** warranting defect closure in ASD or VSD is defined by a pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio **Qp/Qs** at least **1.5:1** with RV volume overload, provided pulmonary vascular resistance is < **3** to **5** Wood units. Severe irreversible pulmonary vascular remodeling with shunt reversal establishes Eisenmenger syndrome, precluding surgical closure.
steps.say: Significant left-to-right shunt warranting defect closure in ASD or VSD is defined by a pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio Qp/Qs at least 1 point 5:1 with RV volume overload, provided pulmonary vascular resistance is less than 3 to 5 Wood units. Severe irreversible pulmonary vascular remodeling with shunt reversal establishes Eisenmenger syndrome, precluding surgical closure.

nodes.label: Calculate Shunt Ratio via Oximetry Run: Qp/Qs
PVR < 3 to 5 Wood Units -> Defect Closure Indicated

steps.tx: **Patent ductus arteriosus** connects the proximal descending aorta to the roof of the main pulmonary artery, presenting with a continuous **machinery murmur** at the left infraclavicular area and wide pulse pressure. Large shunts produce left atrial and left ventricular enlargement, managed with transcatheter coil or plug embolisation.
steps.say: Patent ductus arteriosus connects the proximal descending aorta to the roof of the main pulmonary artery, presenting with a continuous machinery murmur at the left infraclavicular area and wide pulse pressure. Large shunts produce left atrial and left ventricular enlargement, managed with transcatheter coil or plug embolisation.

left.title: Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA)
points: Continuous machinery murmur peaking at S2
Produces left atrial and left ventricular volume overload
High bounding pulses with widened pulse pressure
Differential cyanosis when Eisenmenger syndrome occurs

right.title: Atrial Septal Defect (ASD)
points: Midsystolic pulmonary ejection murmur + fixed split S2
Produces right atrial and right ventricular volume overload
Normal pulse pressure and peripheral pulses
Generalized symmetric cyanosis with shunt reversal

steps.tx: **Coarctation of the aorta** typically occurs near the insertion of the ligamentum arteriosum, manifesting with upper extremity hypertension, **radiofemoral pulse delay**, rib notching involving ribs **3** to **8**, and figure-3 sign on chest radiograph. Percutaneous balloon angioplasty with covered stent implantation represents the primary adult interventional therapy.

rows: Delayed systolic wave arrival distal to stenosis
Seen along inferior borders of ribs 3 to 8
Pre-stenotic dilation, coarctation indentation, post-stenotic dilation

steps.tx: **Cor triatriatum** sinistrum is a rare congenital anomaly where the left atrium is divided into **two** chambers by a **fibromuscular membrane**, mimicking mitral stenosis with pulmonary venous congestion. Surgical resection of the obstructing fibromuscular membrane relieves pulmonary hypertension and achieves complete cure.
